sent_to_model:
Mikaela from our discussion group has asked on the whatsapp how we've got on with 10 in 7 milking this season. I owe her a proper answer, she helped us heaps when Dave did his shoulder. My thumbs are useless on the phone so can you write my reply from what I've put down. Be straight with her about the bad bits too, I don't want to talk her into it and then she blames me in March

- 290 cows, 3-way crossbreds mostly, started 10 in 7 on 21 Sept after mating started
- we skip Tues, Thurs and Sat arvo milkings plus Sunday arvo, so 4 once-a-days a week. Mornings 5.15 every day
- milksolids down about 6% on same weeks last year going off the Fonterra app, rep had said expect 8-10
- SCC jumped from 110k to about 180k first 3 weeks, back around 135k now
- lame cows way down, 4 on the lame list now vs 11 this time last year. long walk to back paddocks is 1.8km
- first skipped Sunday arvo Dave and me went to Hamilton to see the grandkids, first Sunday off in spring in 20 odd yrs
- had a heifer with mastitis go bad on a skipped arvo, didn't spot it till next morning, lost a quarter
- Kieran (our 2IC) said its the first spring he hasn't wanted to quit by October
- cows came round quicker than I thought, about 4 days of bellowing at the gate then fine
- you have to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days or it bites you
- honestly wouldn't go back, the hours alone are worth the 6%
- if Tom's knees are bad the arvos off will help more than anything
- tell her to come look at the shed rosters/numbers at the field day on the 19th
- say ring me if she wants, easier than texting
